data.description:
### 1. Technical Environment

* **code_version:** 1fb0cfd320 (worktree-20260520-153616 after mktemp fix)
* **related tickets:** epic a03c-d55e-1393-4f27 (Closure Checks migration); story ad70-f38a-7684-4e00 (classifier helper); bug 9894-a463-090a-43e5 (CLI alias rejection, referenced in original handoff)

### 2. Incident Overview

* **Scenario Type:** User-Flagged Behavior

#### Expected Behavior

After completing all per-batch migration runs of the classifier helper across the full set of brainstorm:complete-tagged epics, the re-derived pending set should be empty — every brainstorm:complete epic should carry a CLOSURE_CHECKS_CLASSIFIER_AUDIT comment.

#### Actual Behavior

After processing 96 epics across 9 migration batches in this session, 12 IDs remain in the re-derived pending set. They split into two distinct failure classes.

Class A — Archived epics with empty descriptions (5 IDs): 8a5b-e07b, be38-5524, cd3c-2faa, d000-2598, e136-0ec7. For these, `ticket show` returns valid JSON but the description field is empty. The classifier script rejects them with ERROR: <id> could not read description. They remain tagged brainstorm:complete but have no SC content to classify.

Class B — Non-canonical / alias-style IDs the CLI rejects (7 IDs): dso-3xhk, dso-g10j, dso-gkct, dso-khl2, dso-t7af, dso-to7x, w21-bsnz. For these, `ticket show <id>` returns a ticket_not_found error. The IDs appear in `ticket list --type=epic --include-archived` (which is how the pending-set re-derivation discovered them), but `ticket show` cannot resolve them. This is the same failure mode flagged in open bug 9894-a463-090a-43e5 (CLI alias rejection): the alias-style IDs only resolve under their canonical UUIDs, which the listing helper does not expose.

### 3. Action History

1. Session resumed Phase 4 bulk migration on epic a03c-d55e-1393-4f27.
2. Re-derivation produced a 63-epic pending set.
3. Batches 6-10 processed the pending set: 84 successful audits + 12 failures.
4. Final re-derivation returned the 12 unresolvable IDs above.
5. Manual probing via ticket show confirmed the two failure classes.

### 4. Chronological Rationalization

Class A is a content gap, not a tooling bug — these epics carry brainstorm:complete but never had SCs written to migrate. They are operationally done for migration but the audit comment is missing. Options: (a) patch the classifier script to write an empty audit when the description is empty (mirrors the existing items=0 early-exit path), (b) manually post a one-time audit comment for each of the 5 IDs, (c) untag brainstorm:complete from these archived empties so they fall out of the pending set.

Class B is the upstream 9894-a463 problem. The fix lives there. In the meantime, the migration cannot close a03c Phase 4 to 100% without resolving Class B.

### 5. Skills and Workflows

* affected: closure-checks-classifier-pass.sh empty-description detection
* affected: ticket CLI alias resolution depends on 9894-a463-090a-43e5
* affected: epic a03c-d55e-1393-4f27 cannot close at 100% Phase 4 coverage until both classes resolve

#### Suggested fix

1. Class A: extend the classifier script's items=0 early-exit path to also handle empty descriptions — write a stub audit instead of erroring out. ~5-line change. Converts 5 unresolvable IDs into trivially-completed audits.
2. Class B: defer to 9894-a463-090a-43e5. Once that bug ships, these 7 IDs will resolve via their canonical UUIDs and the migration script can process them.
data.title: closure-checks migration: 12 unresolvable IDs in pending set (5 archived empty-desc + 7 non-canonical aliases) -> 100% migration completion blocked
